title: Logic gates (Boolean algebra)
summary: The fundamental logic gates: AND (output 1 if all inputs 1), OR (output 1 if any input 1), NOT (inverter), NAND (NOT AND), NOR (NOT OR), XOR (exclusive OR, output 1 if inputs differ), XNOR (equivalence, output 1 if inputs same). NAND and NOR are universal gates (can implement any Boolean function). De Morgan's laws: NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B; NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B.

structure.meaning: Output = 1 iff all inputs are 1. Truth table: 00->0, 01->0, 10->0, 11->1.
Output = 1 iff any input is 1. Truth table: 00->0, 01->1, 10->1, 11->1.
Output = NOT (A AND B). Universal gate. Truth table: 00->1, 01->1, 10->1, 11->0.
Output = NOT (A OR B). Universal gate. Truth table: 00->1, 01->0, 10->0, 11->0.
Output = 1 iff inputs differ. Truth table: 00->0, 01->1, 10->1, 11->0. (A XOR B = A'B + AB')
Output = 1 iff inputs same (equivalence). Truth table: 00->1, 01->0, 10->0, 11->1.
NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B. NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B.
A AND (A OR B) = A. A OR (A AND B) = A.
A AND (B OR C) = (A AND B) OR (A AND C). A OR (B AND C) = (A OR B) AND (A OR C).

notes: NAND and NOR are universal: any Boolean function can be built from NANDs (or NORs) alone.
XOR is used for parity, checksums, and addition (sum bit).
In CMOS: NAND is faster than AND (fewer transistors in the pull-down network).
A NOT gate is an inverter: 1 PMOS + 1 NMOS transistor.
Boolean algebra is the mathematical foundation of all digital logic.
